extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian agents; Commissioner of Indian Affairs; federal Indian agency administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting template and substantive topics to cover in an annual report from a United States Indian agency: population, schools, medical and sanitary conditions, religion, crime, agriculture, industry, improvements, finances, and recommendations for departmental action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schools (number, management, and attendance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the number and type of schools (day vs. boarding), who manages them (e.g., Sisters of Charity), names of schools, teachers' names and background, and average attendance during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include vocational instruction provided (boys: farming/mechanics; girls: cooking, washing, garment-making), any new schools opened (location), and teacher details (race/color, where educated). Provide attendance figures (monthly averages) and note causes for changes (disease, seasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Education outcomes and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the progress and results of boarding and day schools and the broader social influence of school attendees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note rapidity and thoroughness of progress, numbers educated, the role of boarding-school alumni as centers of influence spreading 'civilized' manners, and any declines in attendance due to illness or other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary and medical conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Document sanitary conditions by season, prevalence of disease, physician activity, and limitations in treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report specific epidemics/illnesses, physician efforts, geographic challenges (wide distances), adequacy of nursing and medicine administration, and whether traditional medicine-men are being consulted. Recommend establishment of a reservation hospital if necessary and explain how lack of facilities undermines confidence in government medical care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion and religious composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for the religious affiliations (numbers per denomination), level of devotion, and general religious sentiment among the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate dominant denomination (e.g., Roman Catholic), numbers affiliated, degree of devoutness, persistence of traditional practices among elders, and the agent's view on religion's role in 'civilization' of the tribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crime, law enforcement, and causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Report breaches of conduct, serious crimes (e.g., murders), policing actions, and proximate causes of criminal incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include counts of misconduct reported by police forces, descriptions of incidents (e.g., drunkenness-related murders), arrests made, policing efficiency, and any recommendations to reduce causes (e.g., liquor control).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness and liquor traffic (problem and remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe prevalence of drunkenness, methods by which liquor is introduced, prosecutions, and recommended legal or policy remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail evasive devices used by saloon-keepers, list prosecutions and sentences, argue for stricter penalties/limiting judicial discretion (e.g., remove light penalties) to deter sellers, and document ongoing impact on the tribe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agriculture: acreage, crops, implements, and yields
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for cultivated acreage, crop types and quantities, agricultural implements owned, and estimates of production both by Indians and government account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific production numbers (e.g., bushels of wheat/oats/barley), estimates of tribal aggregate production, description of community farming patterns (large farms vs many small plots), and government-farmed outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allotment and land-tenure recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss allotments of land to individuals as a policy goal and the effects or expected effects on industry and welfare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether allotments have been made (number/size), argue for or against making allotments (as incentives to industry), note concerns about taxation/sale/judicial claims, and recommend congressional or departmental action (e.g., patents, sale of surplus timber and reinvestment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilized occupations and home industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe non-agricultural employment and home industries (logging camps, sawmill, shingles, drying berries, curing salmon, etc.) and their economic outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include production figures (e.g., shingles made, lumber sawed, cords of wood sold), typical occupations and seasonal labor patterns, and assessment of Indians' competence relative to white workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment, labor, and wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on employes (agency staff) and Indian labor: who is working, nature of employment, and compensation arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note employes' diligence and role in instructing Indians, the use of Indians to perform public works (paid in annuities at stated daily rates), and any government employment (e.g., building public works, reclamation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements and infrastructure projects
rubrics_metrics.description: List improvements completed or underway (school additions, new schoolhouses, storehouses, wharves, saw-mill reconstruction, roads, dams, cooking ranges, houses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe dimensions, construction quality (painted, planed rustic), who performed the work (Indians vs. contractors), sources of materials (manufactured at agency), and costs or payment method (annuities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Present work and reclamation projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe current labor projects (e.g., reclaiming marshland, deepening creek beds) including scope, methods, and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State land area, proposed engineering works (deepening creek 3–4 feet), nature of substrate (gravelly cement), manpower used, and observed progress/pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needed repairs and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report structural deficiencies and maintenance needs (rotted foundations, need for reshingling, incomplete saw-mill) and staffing/resources required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prioritized repair plans, request authority/funding for extra carpenters and labor (with estimates of required personnel), and identify buildings needing immediate attention before winter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency transportation and access/communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Document accessibility of reservations and recommended improvements in roads, bridges, and transport routes that affect agency operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide travel routes (water/rail/team), costs for regular transport (e.g., steamboat cost), recommend road/bridge projects to improve year-round access, and estimate funding needs for road improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency resource management and annuity/fund accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide breakdown of annuity funds and departmental disbursement responsibilities (amounts for education, farming, blacksmith, goods, per-capita money).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Itemize annuity categories and totals, indicate which portions the agent disburses vs. department, and list employe salaries paid from these funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timber and forest resource policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Report on timber valuation, desire for sale of pine, and recommended terms (e.g., give purchasers years to remove lumber and allot lands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include estimates of timber volume and monetary value, tribe's reluctance to sell land, suggested plan (sale then invest proceeds for tribe), and timeline recommendations for purchasers to remove lumber.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and community building
rubrics_metrics.description: Report construction of farm-houses and community structures (churches, barns) built by Indians with or without government assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide counts of houses built, descriptions (first-class, painted), location, and account of government vs. Indian-contributed materials and labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boarding-school attendance factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain causes for lower-than-expected boarding-school attendance and its consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite causes such as measles/whooping-cough or seasonal factors, provide attendance averages, and assess the influence of boarding-school graduates on community assimilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social policy recommendations (relocation, citizenship, patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make policy recommendations to Congress or the department (e.g., confer citizenship, remove bands, issue patents, relocate tribes to better reserves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue for specific legislative or administrative steps, explain consequences of inaction (distrust when patents delayed), and recommend concrete relocation or patenting actions with rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prisoner and special population management
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe status and management of special groups (e.g., Piute and Bannock prisoners), including effects on agency resources and recommended courses of action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report behavior, work activity, schooling of prisoners, how uncertainty about departmental intentions affects morale, and recommend immediate steps for protection, transportation, subsistence, or permanent settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative economic reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific quantitative measures of economic activity and values (lumber feet sawed, shingles made, cords sold, tons of hay, bushels of grain, hay values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both government-account and Indian-account yields and estimated monetary values (per ton or total), plus estimates when exact counts are difficult, with explanation of methods used to estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for agency technical staff (farmers, blacksmiths)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the presence or absence of technical staff (farmers, blacksmiths, teachers) on reservations and request additional staff where needed to promote agriculture and industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State existing employes and their salaries, argue for placement of farmers at specific reserves, and explain how a resident farmer would accelerate progress (example: Lac de Flambeau).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of assimilation and moral/cultural criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer an evaluative judgment about the tribe's commitment to 'civilization' and moral change, often tied to acceptance of Christianity and abandonment of old practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss prevalence of Christian belief, persistence of superstitions among elders, and the agent's conviction that embracing Christian tenets is pivotal for permanent advance; use this to justify educational and religious efforts.
